details:
SPHERESCAPE – Beyond What the Eyes Can See

SPHERESCAPE is a web-based astronomical data exploration platform inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission. Its goal is to make complex infrared astronomical observations easier to discover, access, and explore through an interactive and user-friendly interface.

The platform allows users to search for celestial objects using object names or sky coordinates. It connects with NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) datasets to retrieve SPHEREx archival observations. Users can explore observations across different dates and spectral bands, view observation timelines, wavelength coverage, metadata, and access links to the underlying FITS data.

Benefits and intended impact:
SPHERESCAPE aims to reduce the difficulty of navigating large astronomical datasets by presenting scientific information in a more organised and accessible format. It can support students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers who want to explore infrared observations without having to manually navigate multiple archive resources. The broader intention is to encourage curiosity about space science and make publicly available astronomical data easier to engage with.

Tools and technologies used:

  • Programming language: Python
  • Backend: Flask
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
  • Astronomy and data processing: Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas
  • Data source: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) and SPHEREx archival data
  • Development environment: Visual Studio Code

Creativity and innovation:
The creative aspect of SPHERESCAPE lies in bringing astronomical archive exploration into a single web-based experience. Instead of treating observations as isolated scientific files, the platform organises them by celestial target, observation date, and spectral band, helping users understand how observations are distributed across time and wavelength. It combines real scientific datasets with an accessible interface to make infrared astronomy feel less intimidating and more interactive.

Factors considered during development:
The project considered accessibility, ease of navigation, the organisation of large datasets, accurate presentation of scientific metadata, and the complexity of astronomical coordinates and wavelength information. It also prioritises using publicly available NASA data and presenting the retrieved information in a way that users can understand and explore.

SPHERESCAPE was developed independently for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the team name ASTRAVIA. It is currently a working prototype, with further features and refinements planned.
